candidate_name: Progressive Energy / ElcaTex Group gas-conversion (potential second LNG import path)
sponsor_or_proposer: Progressive Energy (energy arm of ElcaTex Group); MAN Energy Solutions (engine supplier)
current_state: Operating 54.8 MW combined-heat-and-power plant (three MAN 18V51/60 engines) serving an ElcaTex textile facility in Honduras, commissioned ~2018-2019 on heavy fuel oil. Progressive Energy has publicly stated intent to convert the engines to natural gas 'as soon as a secure supply of LNG becomes available.' No dedicated LNG import terminal of its own is proposed; this is a gas-DEMAND signal, not a terminal proposal.
missing_threshold_elements: No terminal sponsor for an import facility (the plant would draw LNG from a third-party supply, not build/own a terminal); no terminal location distinct from the existing Puerto Cortes terminal; no concrete terminal step (no FSRU charter, no permit, no site lease for a second import point). Fails all three discovery-threshold elements as a TERMINAL candidate.
watch_for: Whether Progressive Energy/ElcaTex pursues a dedicated LNG receiving/regas point on the north coast rather than offtake from Genesis's Puerto Cortes terminal; any FSRU charter or onshore regas filing tied to ElcaTex; or a north-coast cluster (Puerto Cortes / San Pedro Sula) of new gas-fired conversions implying additional import capacity beyond Brassavola.
notes: Surfaced via trade-press ring (New Energy Events 'Honduras to have new LNG power engines project soon', which 403s; corroborated by power-eng.com and man-es.com, both URL-verified PASS). Separate signal: USTDA-hosted Honduras Natural Gas Infrastructure Reverse Trade Mission (Meridian International Center, https://meridian.org/project/honduras-natural-gas-opportunities-reverse-trade-mission-and-business-briefing/ , verified PASS) — Honduran energy secretariat/regulator/ENEE delegation met U.S. LNG suppliers; government-level interest in additional north-coast import infrastructure but no named second terminal yet. Re-check ~2026-12. The only concrete Honduras LNG terminal (Puerto Cortes LNG Terminal, Genesis Energias, FSU Bilbao Knutsen, supplying Brassavola CCGT) is ALREADY in GEM (T100001061417).
